Hi Sofia / Martin - thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Need: EU-only data residency for inference requests and logs; procurement will require KMS/HSM integration and SOC2 evidence.
- Workloads: real-time transaction enrichment (latency sensitive) + nightly batch indexing (throughput).
- Deployment modes under consideration: Hosted API (EU region), Dedicated reserved capacity (EU-only, private pools), Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict network controls.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Is EU-region Hosted API acceptable provided data, model execution, and logs remain in EU (no cross-region routing)?
2) Will procurement accept a Hosted offering with contract language and KMS integration, or do you need Dedicated/Private for legal controls?
3) Any internal compliance/infosec checklist we should review before the SE call?

Attachments: call notes stub (aditya-call-notes.txt). I can share SOC2 summary and a high-level deployment diagram in the next email (looping Marissa to handle the technical deep-dive).

Proposed next step: Marissa to set up a 45-minute technical session next week to map network/KMS requirements and confirm whether Hosted EU covers your control needs.

Thanks,

Hi Aditya - thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: All production data and logs must remain in the EU. No cross-border export of transaction data or derived artifacts.
- We have an internal procurement requirement for customer-managed keys (KMS) or HSM-based key wrapping; please confirm support and details.
- Latency: we need sub-100ms p95 for the real-time path; if using Hosted, we need to confirm EU-region latency will meet this.

Can you send SOC2 evidence and a network/deployment diagram showing where data resides and how it flows between components? Legal is CC'd and will want to review. If Hosted requires any cross-region model fallback, that would be a blocker - please be explicit about cross-region routing policies.

Thanks,

Martin / Sofia - appreciate the clear requirements. Quick answers and attached evidence:

- SOC2: attached is a SOC2_summary.pdf (redacted). We can provide the full report under NDA / controlled access.
- EU-only Hosted: Redwood supports an EU-hosted region (eu-west-1) where inference and logs remain in-region. By default our Hosted API will not route user inference to non-EU regions; we can include contractual language to guarantee EU-only processing for your account.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and can accommodate HSM-backed key wrapping for higher assurance - SE will confirm exact flows.
- Cross-region routing: there are model-variant fallbacks we use for capacity/backoff. For strict residency we offer two options: Dedicated reserved capacity (EU-only, private GPU pools, no cross-region fallback) or Private VPC/on-prem (full customer-controlled networking and no outbound routing).
- Latency: Hosted EU typically meets sub-100ms p95 for EU-based clients for standard models; if you need ironclad latency SLAs, Dedicated is recommended.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf, deployment_diagram.png
Links: https://app.redwood.example/docs/regions#eu

Next steps:
- Marissa (cc) to schedule a technical deep-dive early next week to map KMS/network flows and confirm whether Dedicated or Private is required.
- If Legal wants the full SOC2, send an intake and we'll provide controlled access.

Best,
Aditya

Subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency - NordBank follow-up

Hi Martin / Sofia - looping in more technical detail and proposed MAP (mutual action plan). Forwarding our recap below for context.

Summary of deployment options (short):
- Hosted (EU region):
  - Pros: fastest to production, usage-based pricing, supports EU-only processing and logs when account is pinned to EU region.
  - Controls: contractual residency guarantee available; KMS integration for encrypting stored artifacts (we can support customer-managed KMS).
  - Caveat: hosted model-variant fallback may exist; for strict "no fallback" residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Pros: dedicated GPU pools in your chosen region (EU), no cross-region fallback, stronger latency SLOs, can be provisioned with private networking.
  - Controls: dedicated tenancy, expanded logging/audit retention, optional private peering.
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Pros: full network control, air-gapped options, customer-managed keys, supports on-prem deployment if required for regulatory reasons.
  - Controls: full KMS/HSM integration, audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM, and support for long-term retention per policy.

Requested attachments: SOC2 (attached by Aditya), and I've added a short PDF comparative summary and a draft MAP for NordBank (attached MAP-NordBank.xlsx).

Proposed MAP and next calls:
1) 2026-03-02 10:00 CET - Tech deep-dive (Marissa + Vivek) to map KMS and network flow (45m).
2) Legal intake: we'll provide controlled access to the full SOC2 after NDA - Legal (NordBank) to confirm point of contact.
3) If Dedicated is preferred, we'll provide a pricing estimate and provisioning timeline post-tech-call.

Please confirm the 03-02 slot or propose alternatives. Happy to adjust to your procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
